question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}(x+2), & \,1\le x\le 3, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{y}, & \,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡4, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(1\le X\le 2,Y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2).$
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(x+2)\cdot \frac{1}{3}{e}^{y} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}(x+2){e}^{y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [1,3]\times [0,\operatorname{ln}⁡4].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{24}(x+2){e}^{y}, & \,1\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le X\le 2,Y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡2) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{1}{24}(x+2){e}^{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{24}(x+2)[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{24}(x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{24}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+2x)]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}(2+4)-\frac{1}{24}(\frac{1}{2}+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-\frac{5}{48} \\  & =\frac{7}{48}.\end{aligned}
$$
